newsitem.title: USA: Passers-by run off with bags of money from truck.
newsitem.headline: Passers-by run off with bags of money from truck.

text.p: Passers-by took off with bags of money when the door of an armoured truck burst open in a traffic accident on Thursday, officials said.

The red and white truck owned by Armed Courier Service of San Jose, Calif., overturned on a busy street in Oakland after it was involved in a collision with a car, company president Dan Connolly told Reuters.
The back door of the truck flung open, but the two security guards, who were not hurt, were trapped in the cab for several minutes.

In the time it took for police to arrive, passers-by scooped up bags of coins and cash from the back of the truck as well as a few bags that fell out on the street, said Connolly, who described it as "a crime of opportunity" for people in the area.

Connolly said he did not know how much money the truck was carrying or how much was missing. But he said the missing amount was "substantially less" than the $1 million as some news reports had speculated.
Some money bags were left in the truck, which had been collecting money from local businesses, he said.
Local television news said Oakland police detained about six people for questioning, but most of the money was gone.
Connolly said that people who "may have used some poor judgment" and taken money would not face retribution if they voluntarily returned it to Oakland police by Monday evening.
But anyone found with some of the loot would be arrested and prosecuted, he said.

The incident was similar to one in Miami in January when a Brink's armoured truck believed to be carrying $3.7 million flipped on a highway overpass, sending a stream of currency and coins onto a street below. Some local residents grabbed bags and rakes to scoop up the loot on that occasion.
